summary: Add an env-gated disposable Citus/Postgres workload migration harness for the FD-001 messenger, mail, social, and community backbone write plans.
claim_boundary: This slice adds an env-gated integration harness that applies the existing messenger, mail, social, and community Postgres/Citus migration bundles to a disposable Citus target, validates a separate non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS runtime app role, grants only workload schema/table privileges, executes architecture-compliant app-style API/usecase/adapter/outbox write plans for two synthetic tenants from a foundry app harness crate, verifies tenant A/tenant B/no-tenant RLS counts for 13 workload tables, verifies Citus distribution metadata for every workload table, and claims expected protocol outbox rows through the SQLx outbox drain under tenant RLS context. It also relocates the harness out of the SQLx adapter crate to preserve adapter boundary rules, removes the misplaced peer-service dev-dependencies from that adapter, fixes social timestamp bind casts discovered by the live run, and narrows the dependency-seam rationale so the env-gated foundry harness app may declare existing sqlx/tokio test-runtime dependencies without weakening kernel/domain/usecase isolation. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the future dogfood substrate context only. This does not claim a production database, production credentials, production tenant data, live Oyatie Cloud substrate, production tenant workload deployment, backup/restore, Citus rebalance/failover, Kubernetes admission, ArgoCD sync/health, OpenCost allocation, remote CI green, or production SLO evidence.

source_basis.use: Official PostgreSQL row-security behavior: enabled RLS requires policies, default-deny applies when no policy exists, FORCE RLS can subject owners to policies, and superuser/BYPASSRLS roles bypass row security.
Official Citus DDL reference for create_distributed_table, colocate_with, pg_dist_partition metadata, and cautions about combining Citus distributed operations with transaction blocks.

Upstream SQLx raw_sql documentation for raw multi-statement execution behavior; the harness uses split single-statement execution after the disposable Citus run exposed multi-utility transaction limitations.

facets.F1_simplicity: The harness is a single opt-in integration test in a dedicated foundry app crate, reusing service-owned migration constants and composing existing API/usecase/adapter/outbox seams instead of teaching an individual adapter crate about peer adapters.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The slice moves from static SQL/app-plan assertions to disposable Citus-backed tenant isolation evidence for the four FD-001 backbone services that are intended to run later as Oyatie Cloud tenant workloads.
facets.F3_adversarial: TDD began with compile failures for the missing workload live config, table inventory, app-plan builder, and harness runner. Disposable Citus runs exposed multi-utility migration execution limits and a social timestamp bind mismatch; full verifier runs exposed both an adapter-boundary violation from misplaced dev-dependencies and strict dependency-seam sqlx/tokio allowlist blocks, so the harness was relocated into an app-role crate and the dependency rationale was bounded to that env-gated harness before final verification.
facets.F4_api_contract: No production service API changes are introduced. The public SQLx command executor API remains unchanged. The outbox SQLx drain keeps its public request/config API while adding the required tenant RLS session setting inside claim/mutation transactions.
facets.F5_quality: Focused tests/checks passed for the foundry workload harness app, SQLx command adapter, SQLx outbox adapter, and social Postgres adapter. The live integration test is disabled unless explicitly enabled, while default tests still compile and validate the harness inventory and write-plan construction.
facets.F6_operations: Operators must provide setup/admin and app/runtime DSNs separately. The harness validates app role posture, cleans disposable schemas, applies migrations, grants runtime privileges, runs synthetic tenant workloads, checks distribution metadata, and cleans up schemas afterward.
facets.F7_security_privacy: No credentials, DSNs, or production tenant data are stored. Live-run commands in evidence redact DSNs. The app role must not be superuser, must not have BYPASSRLS, and must differ from the setup role before isolation can be claimed.
facets.F8_supply_chain: No new third-party dependency is introduced. Cargo.lock changes are from a new path-only workspace harness crate and path-only dev-dependencies that let the foundry app integration test construct existing workload plans and outbox claim requests. The existing sqlx/tokio dependency rationale now explicitly scopes their use to this env-gated foundry live workload harness app while keeping kernel/domain/usecase crates runtime-free.
facets.F9_testing: Default tests cover env gating, required app URL, workload table inventory, and six write plans per tenant. A disposable Citus 13.0 container run exercised migrations, Citus distribution metadata, tenant RLS counts, app-role separation, SQL execution, and outbox claims.
facets.F10_ci_cd: The live workload harness is CI-safe by default because it returns early unless explicitly enabled through environment variables. Architecture-boundary and strict dependency-seam gates now pass because peer-service adapter/usecase dependencies live in an app-role harness crate, while sqlx/tokio use is documented as env-gated harness-only rather than domain/usecase leakage.
facets.F11_observability: The live report records migrations applied, write plans executed, outbox batches claimed, distribution/app-role check flags, app role name, and per-table visibility counts for tenant A, tenant B, and no-tenant scopes.
facets.F13_reversibility: The slice is isolated to a dedicated harness app crate, path dev-dependency wiring, an outbox transaction RLS setting, and a narrow social timestamp cast fix. Reverting it removes the live workload harness without changing domain/API/usecase contracts.
